title: Two-cycle ear theorem
statement: If C is a simple cycle of length r and P is a C-ear of length p whose endpoints divide C into arcs of lengths a and r-a, then P together with the two arcs gives cycles of lengths p+a and p+r-a.

title: Shortest-cycle ear barrier
statement: If C is a shortest cycle of length r and P is a C-ear of length p with endpoint arc lengths a and r-a, then p>=max(a,r-a)>=ceil(r/2).

title: Shortest ear is induced
statement: A shortest C-ear contains no chord between nonconsecutive vertices of the ear path.

title: Long shortest-ear interior avoids C
statement: Let P=x0...xp be a shortest C-ear with p>=3. No internal vertex of P has a neighbor in C outside the two ear endpoints.

title: Forced escape from a long clean ear
statement: In a graph of minimum degree at least 3, every internal vertex of a p>=3 shortest C-ear has a neighbor outside C union P.

title: Common-neighbor spacing on an ear
statement: If C is a shortest cycle of length r and an outside vertex z is adjacent to ear vertices xi,xj with i<j, then j-i>=r-2.

title: Ear contact multiplicity bound
statement: An outside vertex has at most 1+floor((p-2)/(r-2)) neighbors among the internal vertices of a length-p ear around a shortest r-cycle.

title: Ear-replacement connector barrier
statement: Let Q be an exterior xi-xj connector of length h through one component, with d=j-i. If P is a shortest C-ear, then h>=d.

title: Local-cycle connector barrier
statement: Under the same setup, if C is a shortest cycle of length r then h>=r-d.

title: Double-barrier connector theorem
statement: Every exterior xi-xj connector around a shortest cycle and shortest ear satisfies h>=max(d,r-d)>=ceil(r/2).

title: Three-cycle connector packet
statement: If the base cycle arcs have lengths a,b with a+b=r, then an exterior xi-xj connector Q of length h generates cycles of lengths h+d, h+p-d+a, and h+p-d+b.

title: Ear-tight exchange theorem
statement: If an exterior connector has h=d, replacing the xi-xj segment of a shortest ear by the connector yields another shortest ear of the same length.

title: Cycle-tight exchange theorem
statement: If an exterior connector has h=r-d, its union with the xi-xj ear segment is another shortest cycle of length r.

title: P-to-C return double barrier
statement: If a path Q of length h joins internal ear vertex xi to a base-cycle vertex and is otherwise disjoint from C union P, then h>=max(i,p-i).

title: Four-cycle return packet
statement: A P-to-C return from xi to v creates four cycles, using either ear endpoint and either corresponding arc of C; their lengths are h+i+c, h+i+r-c, h+p-i+e, and h+p-i+r-e.

title: Exterior C-ear barrier
statement: If Q is an exterior path of length h joining two base-cycle vertices whose arc lengths are c and r-c, and P is a shortest C-ear of length p, then h>=max(p,c,r-c).

title: Low-degree attachment theorem
statement: Assume every proper subgraph of a minimum counterexample is 2-degenerate. For every component H outside K=C union P, the induced graph on H plus its attachment set has an attachment vertex of degree at most 2 in that induced graph.

title: Singleton attachment multiplicity bound
statement: Under OE17, if an exterior component attaches to K at only one vertex s, then s has at most two neighbors in that component.

title: Root-neighbor cubic theorem
statement: If a singleton component attaches through a single edge sy, every other component vertex has graph degree at least 3, and the component is 2-degenerate, then d_H(y)=2 and d_G(y)=3.

title: Rooted degeneracy-wave ordering
statement: Under OE19, the singleton component has a 2-degeneracy elimination ordering beginning with y; every later vertex that first becomes removable has lost a neighbor earlier in the ordering.

title: Single-ear dyadic forcing is false
statement: A shortest cycle together with one ear need not generate a power-of-two cycle.

title: Bare expansion is not a finite contradiction
statement: Exponential local branching around a shortest cycle does not by itself contradict finiteness of a hypothetical counterexample.

title: One connector packet is insufficient
statement: The double barriers and the three-cycle packet for a single connector do not force a dyadic cycle.

title: Power-of-two difference forcing is false
statement: Arbitrarily large integer attachment sets may avoid all power-of-two pairwise differences.

title: Complete ordinary-ear closure theorem
statement: Every finite minimum-degree-at-least-3 completion of the complete ear system around a shortest non-dyadic cycle creates a power-of-two cycle.

title: C4-free cubic-neighborhood matching
statement: In a C4-free graph, the subgraph induced by the three neighbors of a cubic vertex has maximum degree at most 1.

title: Valid suppression neighbor exists
statement: At every cubic vertex y in a C4-free graph, one neighbor a is nonadjacent to the other two neighbors b,c.

title: Y-to-V suppression preserves minimum degree
statement: Delete a cubic vertex y with neighbors a,b,c where ab and ac are absent, and add ab,ac. The resulting simple graph has minimum degree at least 3 whenever the original graph does.

title: Suppression cycle-lift dictionary
statement: For the Y-to-V suppression centered at neighbor a, a cycle using zero artificial edges lifts unchanged, a cycle using both artificial edges lifts with the same length, and a cycle using exactly one artificial edge lifts to a cycle one edge longer.

title: Single-artificial-edge obstruction
statement: In a minimum-order counterexample, every dyadic cycle in a valid suppressed graph uses exactly one artificial edge.

title: Near-dyadic cycle at every cubic vertex
statement: Every cubic vertex of a minimum-order counterexample lies on a cycle of length 2^k+1 for some k>=2.

title: Mersenne path certificate
statement: For every cubic vertex y in a minimum-order counterexample, two of its neighbors are joined in G-y by a simple path of length 2^k-1.

title: Triangle-completion suppression
statement: If a cubic vertex has an independent neighborhood {a,b,c}, deleting it and adding the triangle ab,bc,ca gives a smaller simple graph of minimum degree at least 3.

title: Triangle-completion one-edge obstruction
statement: In a minimum-order counterexample with independent cubic neighborhood, every dyadic cycle in the triangle-completed graph uses exactly one added triangle edge.

title: Local Mersenne coverage theorem
statement: For an independent cubic neighborhood {a,b,c}, at least one of the three neighbor pairs has a path of length 2^k-1 in G-y.

title: Equal-exponent fan kill
statement: If two length-(2^k-1) certificates share one terminal and are internally disjoint away from it, then together with the two edges through the cubic center they form a cycle of length 2^(k+1).

title: Bottleneck complementary-cycle theorem
statement: Two equal-length Mersenne certificates with first common interior vertex split into two simple cycles of lengths s and 2q-s, where q=2^k.

title: Forbidden bottleneck-sum ladder
statement: In a counterexample, the bottleneck sum s in CS12 avoids every value 2^j and 2q-2^j.

title: Same-scale symmetric-difference ledger
statement: For two cycles C1,C2 of length q+1 sharing m edges, the total length of the edge-disjoint cycles in C1 symmetric-difference C2 equals 2(q+1-m).

title: Connected symmetric-difference cycle theorem
statement: If the symmetric difference in CS14 is connected, it is one cycle of length 2(q+1-m).

title: Dyadic overlap-path theorem
statement: Two (q+1)-cycles sharing exactly one path of length s and otherwise edge-disjoint produce a cycle of length 2(q+1-s), dyadic whenever s=q+1-2^j.

title: One-edge local collision theorem
statement: Two equal-exponent suppression cycles at one cubic center that share only their common center edge force a cycle of length 2q.

title: Global exponent repetition
statement: If one Mersenne certificate exponent is chosen at each of M cubic vertices of an n-vertex graph, some exponent occurs at least M/(floor(log2 n)-1) times.

title: Same-scale edge-overlap threshold
statement: In a graph with m edges, more than m/(q+1) distinct cycles of length q+1 force two cycles to share an edge.

title: Exponent repetition alone is insufficient
statement: Repetition of the same near-dyadic exponent at many cubic vertices does not by itself produce a dyadic cycle.

title: Suppression-spectrum intersection theorem
statement: Across the valid suppressions of a cubic vertex, either one dyadic cycle lifts exactly or two hostile one-edge sectors share an exponent and combine into a dyadic cycle.

title: Cubic suppression branch close
statement: No cubic minimum-order counterexample survives all valid Y-to-V and triangle-completion suppressions.
